results.reasoning: Four of the five steps hold and one does not. The bar reads walkdown / project name / screen picker / Prototype-fade-App / viewport / Pin mode / Start walkdown. `panel.screen-picker` is labelled with the screen the page is ("The review page") without being opened, and opens `panel.screens-list` listing every screen plus a "Detect from the page" reset; picking `rule-detail` by hand relabels the button and marks it btn-outline btn-primary with the title "Screen picked by hand", so detection and a hand pick are told apart from the bar. Prototype and App swap the page area and Pin mode toggles from the bar. What fails is the first step: the project cannot be changed there. `panel.blueprint` is a plain non-interactive <span> holding data.project (lib/viewer/panel.js ~1874) - the only project control is the radio list on the Blueprints tab. Note n-0110 files it, with the observation that n-0017 deliberately dropped a broken project selector from the bar, so this may be a statement that has outlived its build rather than a missing control.

One control and one state. Off, the bar's button is btn-outline btn-primary; armed from the bar it becomes btn-warning (lit) and the framed page takes a crosshair on both body and documentElement. Escape typed at the panel's own chrome ended pin mode: the button returned to btn-outline btn-primary and the frame's cursor went back to auto in the same beat. Nothing inside the frame draws a second pin control - the only walkdown element in the framed document is the embed's own shadow host - so there is no rival switch to fall out of step with the bar.

Judged against a page written for the purpose: sticky header, and a modal at inset:0 with z-index 2147483647. In a 1500x950 window the frame is 1080x894 at (12,44) and the app's own innerWidth/innerHeight read 1080x894 - it is laid out against the sheet, not the window. The modal measured 1080x894 at (0,0) INSIDE that frame, and the sticky header pinned to the frame's top at width 1080: neither reached walkdown's bar, which kept its full 1500x44 across the top and stayed usable. Navigating the frame to another screen moved the panel with it - the screen picker went from the bare page's title to "The review page" with no reload of the host. One step was not exercised: stripping X-Frame-Options and CSP for a page that refuses framing needs the packed extension, whose vendored panel/embed copies are not this working tree. I read it instead - extension/background.js allowFraming() adds a declarativeNetRequest session rule scoped to `tabIds: [tabId]` and `resourceTypes: ['sub_frame']`, added when a review starts and removed when it ends, which is exactly what the step asks - but a person should treat that step as unverified by this run.

On a page carrying zero anchor attributes, pin mode still armed and a click opened the form headed `unanchored spot - no anchored element here - pinned by position`. Filing it wrote a real thread: anchor { screen: bare-app, position: { x: 548, y: 476 }, surface: app, viewport: { name: desktop, width: 1080 } } and no element at all - recorded by where it sits, not against an element. It drew as a positioned pin, `pin.marker` with left/top in pixels rather than an element-bound one. On the fixture that does carry anchors, the same gesture on host.cta opened a form headed `host.cta`: anchored pins are unaffected.

Pointed at a port with nothing listening, the panel says "No blueprints open", explains why a browser tab cannot read a filesystem, and names the command outright in a code block: `walkdown serve`. It reads as a first step rather than an error - explanatory prose, the panel's ordinary primary colouring, no error styling anywhere. The address box carries aria-label "walkdown server address" and holds a URL, not a path, with "Then every blueprint under that folder is listed here" beneath it; typing a live address and pressing Connect brought the whole panel up with no page reload. Once connected the folder is named plainly - "Serving ~/Development/profoundry/walkdown/.walkdown/checkspace - every blueprint under it is listed below" - on the blueprint chooser and on the Blueprints tab.

With embed.pin.anchored-target open in the detail seat (track at translateX(-33.3333%)), the Blueprints tab drew its own content into that seat - server address, folder, and the two projects as radios - with no trace of the rule detail. The Threads tab likewise drew `panel.threads-list` with its filter head. Returning to Rules showed the list again, with the previously opened rule still highlighted and openable. No tab slid past another tab's detail to reach its own.

The counts reconcile with the list exactly. The footer reads 62/86 verified with a tooltip stating the unit ("Rules holding a current pass on every tier they ask for"), and one owed badge, `3 walk`. Scanning all 86 rule rows found exactly three carrying the word walk - panel.rules.one-pane-per-tab, search-the-list, tiers-at-a-glance - and none carrying sign, so the badges sum to the footer kind for kind and the kind with nothing owed draws nothing. The Rules tab carries 3, the same number and the same warning colour as the rule glyphs (both oklch(0.84 0.15 85)); Blueprints, holding nothing for me, draws no badge; Threads counts its own work in badge-info rather than a second yellow. Judging all three during the sitting emptied the tab badge. One wording caveat worth a person's eye: "verified" no longer says "rules" in the visible text - the word now lives only in the tooltip - where the 2026-08-25 evidence cited "24 of 77 rules verified" as the unit stated outright.

Driven over a disposable copy of this blueprint, never the real ledger. Passing panel.rules.one-pane-per-tab opened panel.rules.search-the-list by itself and the tally rose 0/3 -> 1/3. Failing the next kept the rule open so the reason could be written where the rule is, and the tally still counted it. Pin mode was left exactly as found in both directions: off through a fail, and armed before a fail it was still armed after. Judging the last owed rule returned to the list, not a dead end, with a toast reading "Nothing left owing a verdict in this blueprint - Finish walkdown records the sitting". Carrying on is asked for rather than done: `panel.continue` sits beside the tally in `panel.actor`.

Judged on the example blueprint, which is where a screen actually declares a setup - no screen in walkdown's own storyboard carries the field, so its own rules correctly show nothing there. Opening waitlist.join.already-joined, whose screen is the confirmation page told apart by a query, `detail.setup` reads "Join with an email already on the list - the same page comes back saying so", it is labelled Setup (the storyboard's own word, which n-0099 asked for in place of "To Get Here"), and it sits above `detail.steps`. Opening waitlist.join.email-required, on a screen with no setup, `detail.setup` is absent entirely rather than empty.

The Threads tab lists every thread on the blueprint with what it is anchored to above each one - a rule id, two rule ids where a thread is anchored to both, a screen title for one anchored to a screen, and one row anchored to no rule at all. `panel.thread-filter` asks the command line's three questions in its own words and counts them: Active 80, Awaiting you 72, All 109. It is a fixed head rather than the first thing to scroll away - its top stayed at 141px with the list scrolled to 2000px. Asking for all of them reached 18 verified and 8 waived threads, which nothing else in the panel can show. Opening one drew the conversation beside the list, and the way back was the thread list, not a rule nobody opened. The tab itself carries 72 - how many are waiting on a person - so it is legible from whichever tab is open.

One control in the bar owns both halves: "Start walkdown" with nothing running, the same button reading "Finish walkdown" while one runs, so it says what it is. Carrying on is a separate question and sits where the rule says - `panel.continue`, inside `panel.actor`, beside the tally, never in the bar. The tally reads as a fraction (0/3, then 1/3, 2/3, 3/3), so how far in and how much is left are one glance. Continue opened the next rule still owing a verdict rather than the next in list order. Colour follows the rule exactly: the ending is filled warning (btn-warning) and carrying on is outlined warning (btn-outline btn-warning); beginning wears warning while three rules are owed and drops back to btn-primary once nothing is owed, which I saw happen after the last verdict landed. Every count came from one list - the Rules tab's 3, the footer's `3 walk`, the tally's denominator and the rule Continue opened all agreed, and all emptied together.

The desk is drafting paper, not a spreadsheet. `panel.desk` is a dedicated layer at z-index -1 under the page sheet, ruled by two repeating-linear-gradients at 0 and 90 degrees whose ink is color-mix(base-content 10%, transparent) - faint, not hard lines. It lies at an angle and the perspective is real: the inline transform is perspective(600px) rotateX(35deg) rotate(35deg) and the computed value is a matrix3d, not a 2D skew, so the ruling converges toward a horizon the way a sheet on a desk does. Narrowing the frame to the mobile preset, and again with the peek checkbox on, shows that convergence across the whole desk. The flat fallback exists and is reached only when CSS.supports('transform','perspective(1px) rotateX(1deg)') is false, exactly as the rule allows.

Five of six steps hold. The gear opens a tuner with five dials; dragging Tilt repainted the desk live with no reload (rotate(35deg) -> rotate(41deg) under the keys). Each dial's number can be typed: clicking the value turns it into a real number input, Enter commits, and typing 52 into Tip moved the desk to rotateX(52deg). The choice survives the session - localStorage `walkdown:desk` held {tilt:41,...} and a fresh load came back at rotate(41deg). Nothing about it reaches the ledger: the store is localStorage only, no verdict, no run, no thread. It sits one GAP clear of the app frame's corner on both axes, measured dx=12 dy=12. What fails is the closing step. Escape closes it, a click on the sidebar closes it, a click on the bare desk margin closes it, the gear toggles it - but a click inside the application under review does not, and the app is most of "anywhere outside it". The handler is a capturing pointerdown on the panel document, and a pointerdown inside a frame never reaches the parent. Note n-0111 files it, including the existing embed->parent postMessage channel that could carry the missing signal.

Ticking the checkbox dims rather than hides: the app frame and the aside both went to opacity 0.1 together and stayed on screen, so the ruling is judged against the things that sit on top of it rather than against nothing - the whole desk's converging grid is legible through them. The same call covers the headless cover, which is opaque by design (hideApp() dims app, side and headlessCover as one set). The bar stayed at opacity 1 throughout with its buttons and the gear still working, and the tuner itself stayed full strength. Moving a dial with the peek on left the frame at 0.1 - the re-assert after each repaint holds. Closing the tuner with Escape returned everything to full strength, and reopening it the checkbox was unticked again: it is a way of looking, not a preference.

Three states, three right answers, on a server holding two blueprints. Started with no project named on http://localhost:4310/index.html - the address the example blueprint declares - the panel opened walkdown-example without asking, even though walkdown is the project the server serves by default. Started on the same page with bp=blueprint named explicitly, it stayed on walkdown: the address never overrides a caller who said which. Started on an address no blueprint claims, it did not guess - the chooser asked, naming the folder it is serving and listing both projects as options.
